Permutation Test of random or fixed effects for lmer, glmer and glmmTMB models.

Source: R/permlmer.R
permlmer.Rd

This function provides permutation tests for the terms in a linear mixed model of lmer, and in a generalized linear mixed model of glmer or glmmTMB (also as permglmer() and permglmmTMB()).

Usage

permlmer(lmer0, lmer1, nperm = 999, ncore=3, plot=FALSE, seed, perms=NULL,
         method=c("auto", "working", "quantile"))
permglmer(lmer0, lmer1, nperm = 999, ncore=3, plot=FALSE, seed, perms=NULL,
          method=c("auto", "working", "quantile"))
permglmmTMB(lmer0, lmer1, nperm = 999, ncore=3, plot=FALSE, seed, perms=NULL,
            method=c("auto", "working", "quantile"))

Arguments

lmer0

lmer (or glmer, glmmTMB) model under H0, note that lmer0 model must nest within lmer1 model.

lmer1

lmer (or glmer, glmmTMB) model under H1, note that lmer0 model must nest within lmer1 model.

nperm

Number of permutation, the default value is 999.

ncore

Number of core for parallel computing, the default value is 3.

plot

Plot permutation distribution or not, the default value is FALSE.

seed

Specify a random number generator seed, for reproducible results. The user's random number stream is left as it was.

perms

Optional matrix of permutations to use instead of free ones, one row per observation and one column per permutation (e.g. from permindex); nperm is then its number of columns.

method

For GLMMs only: "working" permutes on the working (link) scale, "quantile" permutes quantile residuals of a 0/1 response and refits the GLMMs; "auto" (the default) uses "quantile" for 0/1 responses and "working" otherwise. See Details.

Value

The anova() table of the two models with the permutation p-value in column Perm-p; for GLMMs, attribute "method" says which method was used, and attribute "failures" gives the number of refits that failed and were left out (if any).

Details

The residuals of lmer0 are decorrelated with the symmetric square root of their covariance under lmer0, permuted, correlated again and added to the fitted values of lmer0 (Lee and Braun, 2012); both models are refitted to each permuted data set. The likelihood-ratio statistics are compared after rounding to 4 decimals, so an observed statistic of 0 (the tested variance estimated at 0) gives a p-value of 1. Since predictmeans 2.0 the square root is symmetric, so the results do not depend on the order of the data (1.x used the Cholesky factor).

For GLMMs (glmer or glmmTMB; since predictmeans 2.0), method = "working" does the same on the working (link) scale: lmer0 is linearised at its fit (working response \(z = \eta + (y - \mu) d\eta/d\mu\), working variance \(\phi V(\mu)/(a (d\mu/d\eta)^2)\); the covariance of z also has the random effects, as in R2_glmm), the decorrelated working residuals are permuted, and the statistic is the likelihood-ratio statistic of weighted linear mixed models fitted to the working responses (REML when the two models have the same fixed effects, ML otherwise). In simulations it kept the 5% level for counts and for binomial data with several trials, and was much more robust than the usual likelihood-ratio test when counts were overdispersed. For 0/1 responses the working scale fails when events are rare or clusters tiny (36% rejections at the 5% level), so method = "quantile" is used: randomised quantile residuals (Dunn and Smyth, 1996) of the response given the conditional means of lmer0 are permuted and mapped back to 0/1 responses, and both models are refitted (glmer fits with nAGQ = 0, for the observed data too, so the statistic can differ from the Chisq column); it kept the level (5.6-6.2%). A random effect with one level per observation (often used for overdispersion) cannot be used on the working scale; bootmodels can test it. glmmTMB models must have no zero inflation and the default dispersion model; families poisson, binomial, nbinom1, nbinom2, Gamma, gaussian and beta are handled.

References

Oliver E. Lee and Thomas M. Braun (2012), Permutation Tests for Random Effects in Linear Mixed Models. Biometrics, Journal 68(2).

Peter K. Dunn and Gordon K. Smyth (1996), Randomized Quantile Residuals. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 5(3), 236-244.

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

library(predictmeans)
## Test random effects (99 permutations to keep the example quick;
## use 999 or more in practice)
fm1 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), sleepstudy)
fm2 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject), sleepstudy)
fm3 <- update(fm1, . ~ . - (Days | Subject) + (1 | Subject))
anova(fm1, fm2, fm3)
#> refitting model(s) with ML (instead of REML)
#> Data: sleepstudy
#> Models:
#> fm3: Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)
#> fm2: Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject)
#> fm1: Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)
#>     npar    AIC    BIC  logLik -2*log(L)   Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
#> fm3    4 1802.1 1814.8 -897.04    1794.1                          
#> fm2    5 1762.0 1778.0 -876.00    1752.0 42.0754  1  8.782e-11 ***
#> fm1    6 1763.9 1783.1 -875.97    1751.9  0.0639  1     0.8004    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
# \donttest{
permlmer(fm3, fm2, nperm=99, ncore=1)
#> Data: sleepstudy
#> Models:
#> lmer0: Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject)
#> lmer1: Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject)
#>       npar    AIC    BIC  logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq) Perm-p
#> lmer0    4 1794.5 1807.2 -893.23    1786.5                            
#> lmer1    5 1753.7 1769.6 -871.83    1743.7 42.796  1 6.0763e-11   0.01
permlmer(fm2, fm1, nperm=99, ncore=1)
#> Data: sleepstudy
#> Models:
#> lmer0: Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject)
#> lmer1: Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)
#>       npar    AIC    BIC  logLik -2*log(L) Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq) Perm-p
#> lmer0    5 1753.7 1769.6 -871.83    1743.7                           
#> lmer1    6 1755.6 1774.8 -871.81    1743.6 0.041  1     0.8395   0.91
# }

## Test fixed effects
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm0 <- lmer(yield ~ nitro+Variety+(1|Block/Variety), data=Oats)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety+(1|Block/Variety), data=Oats)
# \donttest{
permlmer(fm0, fm, nperm=99, ncore=1)
#> refitting model(s) with ML (instead of REML)
#> Data: Oats
#> Models:
#> lmer0: yield ~ nitro + Variety + (1 | Block/Variety)
#> lmer1: yield ~ nitro * Variety + (1 | Block/Variety)
#>       npar    AIC    BIC  logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq) Perm-p
#> lmer0    9 616.04 636.53 -299.02    598.04                            
#> lmer1   15 625.91 660.06 -297.95    595.91 2.1375  6    0.90663   0.96

## A GLMM: do tick counts vary between locations, beyond broods?
gm1 <- glmer(TICKS ~ YEAR + scale(HEIGHT) + (1 | BROOD), family = poisson, data = lme4::grouseticks)
gm2 <- glmer(TICKS ~ YEAR + scale(HEIGHT) + (1 | BROOD) + (1 | LOCATION), family = poisson,
             data = lme4::grouseticks)
permglmer(gm1, gm2, nperm = 99, ncore = 1, seed = 1)
#> Data: lme4::grouseticks
#> Models:
#> m0: TICKS ~ YEAR + scale(HEIGHT) + (1 | BROOD)
#> m1: TICKS ~ YEAR + scale(HEIGHT) + (1 | BROOD) + (1 | LOCATION)
#>    npar    AIC    BIC  logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq) Perm-p
#> m0    5 1988.1 2008.1 -989.04    1978.1                            
#> m1    6 1987.9 2011.9 -987.94    1975.9 2.1992  1    0.13809   0.08
# }
